data.name: Light of Mine
data.detailed_description:
Light of Mine is one of the scariest experiences you will have in VR this Halloween. Explore an ancient temple where innocent looking statues come to life, but only when your back is turned.

Use your candle in the darkened temple to find your way and outwit the horrors within. You will spend the rest of your day looking over your shoulder when the headset comes off.

Light of Mine is made by adults on the autism spectrum at nonPareil Studios. We are a studio that provides better futures for adults with autism, providing training in game development, programming, art and design. #PoweredbyAutism

reviews.review:
[h1] Played this on the Oculus Rift with Touch Controllers [/h1]

I was able to play this game on the Oculus, but when I started the game I had this terrible lag in the video.  The graphics would be very laggy and just stutter and even shake.  Making playing the game almost unbearable.  However, I then did a Windows 7 compatibility fix and my major graphical problems were fixed, although the game never ran smoothly.  

Another problem is the button mapping.  You have to press down on the joystick to move forward and backward.  Those are your only options.  You move forward or backward based on where the candle you hold in your right hand is pointing.  So locomotion throughout the game was very frustrating.  Unfortunately, the gameplay requires solid movement controls to be enjoyable.  Also, the activation of switches can be very tricky and annoying.  Sometimes they activated when I didn't want them to and sometimes they didn't completely activate, leading to deaths.

I hestitate go give a time estimate on finishing the game.  Mostly because of the Windows 7 fix, Steam did not accurately gauge my time finishing the game.  But also because of the poor controls and graphical issues, the game took me a lot longer to finish.  I estimate I spent 40 minutes on the game.  I think more than likely there is only 10 minutes of actual gameplay.  

There are 5 stages or levels in the game.  You're basically supposed to light your candle while avoiding these statutes that follow you when you're not looking at them.  If they get too close and you're not looking at them, then it's goodbye time.  You use your flashlight to activate some doors.  You use your lighted candle to light some altars.  The goal is to light every altar and navigate the maze like levels and avoid getting touched by a statute.  There's a creepy atmosphere throughout the game.  

So I obviously spent more time fixing the game than playing the game.  More time dealing with the poor controls rather than enjoying the game.  But it was only .99 cents.  I was surprised by the nice looking environments even though the game ran so poorly that it was difficult to enjoy.  You can tell that a lot of time and effort went into making this game.  You're not going to find many more games with this much for only .99 cents asking price.  

So do I recommend?  Well, if you're on the Oculus Rift: prepare to be frusrated.  The game is probably a lot more enjoyable on the HTC Vive.

Rating 5/10 can be fun, if you're willing to put up with all the problems
